newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a speech to the Confederation of British Industry in London last night, Prime Minister John Howard described European proposals for greenhouse gas reductions as "irrational and unworkable". It was a move that has put him at odds with the British Goverment which is a strong supporter of tough and binding greenhouse gas reduction targets. Page 1.

The announcement yesterday that High Court judge Justice John Toohey will retire in February, two years earlier than required, gives the Federal Government the opportunity to entrench conservative dominance in the Court for the next 20 years, and end its era of judicial activism which has led to controversial decisions such as Mabo and Wik. Page 1.

Political strategists within the Federal Government are moving to take the emphasis in the tax reform debate off a goods and services tax following Federal Treasurer Peter Costello's warning to Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith, who floated the ida of a plebiscite on the issue over the weekend. Page 3.

While the Labor Party has agreed to pass the Federal Government's work-for-the-dole proposal, there is still resistance to the scheme from unions, church groups, and community organisations. The scheme, which faces the tough "Real Jobs, Real Choices" camaign, is expected to commence in October. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Senate last night rejected Federal Government plans for a postal vote to elect delegates to the proposed convention on the republic, leading Government sources to suggest the convention, planned for December, will not go ahead as the elections being insisted on by the Senate could not be held in time. Page 1.

Following an emotional plea at the United Nations by British Prime Minister Tony Blair urging world leaders to embrace binding targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, Prime Minister John Howard attacked the imposition of such targets, labelling them ufair, irrational, and "ultimately unworkable" targets. Page 1.

The Federal Court yesterday found ICI Australia was negligent for manufacturing and producing a feed, sold by ICI as Helix between 1989 and 1994, that led to the chemical contamination of millions of cattle and damaged Australia's beef export market. ICI now faces a multi-million dollar compensation bill to over 400 cattle producers. Page 1.

Victorian Planning Minister Rob Maclellan said yesterday the State Government would not approve the plan to relocate the Coode Island chemical storage plant to Point Lillias. Maclellan said safety upgrades at Coode Island after an explosion in 1991 now made the site suitable. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Olympic Committee chairman and Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games vice-president John Coates is believed to be happy with a proposal by soccer's governing body FIFA to hold the first match of the Olympics two days earlier than the opening ceremony to avoid a strain on players during the Games. The move is a coup for Victoran Premier Jeff Kennett as the first match would be played in Melbourne. Page 1.

In a move signalling a major diplomatic rift between Australia and Britain, Prime Minister John Howard has defied calls by British Prime Minister Tony Blair to fall into line on greenhouse gas emissions, saying Australia will continue to oppose legally biding uniform targets on greenhouse emissions. Page 1.

Justice Murray Wilcox of the Federal Court yesterday ruled chemical giant ICI Australia had, in its rush for profits, cut research corners and suppressed information, and as a result breached its duty of care to graziers who unknowingly used contaminated cotton waste as drought feed. ICI now faces compensation claims of more than A$100 million. Page 1.

Australia's legal system is facing uncertainty after the announcement yesterday of the resignation of High Court judge Justice John Toohey. Toohey's resignation is the fifth in only three years, and hands the Coalition Government the opportunity to favourably reshape the Court. Page 1.
THE AGE

Environmentalists, the Federal Government and residents were surprised yesterday by a Victorian Government turnaround that will see the Coode Island chemical storage plant remain in its present location. Plans to relocate the plant to Point Lillias were abandoned because of ecological and Aboriginal heritage concerns. Page 1.

In what will be the most significant change in the Family Court in 20 years, the Federal Government is expected to allow reporting of Family Court cases, which would also allow the naming and photographing of parties involved. However, custody cases, allegations and evidence will remain suppressed to avoid sensationalised reporting. Page 1.

Federal Labor's backbench has criticised its leader Kim Beazley over the Opposition's apparent turnaround on the work-for-the-dole scheme. Beazley admitted to the party room that the decision to side with the Government on the scheme was based on electoral panic. Page 1.

A Victorian Department of Human Services spokesman said yesterday about 40 prisoners at Fulham Prison, a 600-bed men's private prison near Sale, were being tested for tuberculosis after one prisoner believed to have contracted the infectious disease was moved to hospital. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
